rules.label: Presumptive eligibility via state/federal programs
rules.quote: Presumptive Eligibility: Eligibility in state or federally funded programs. Examples include housing assistance, food stamps and the Women, Infants & Children program (WIC).

notes: Policy applies only to Vail Health medical bills; services by other providers (Vail Valley Surgery Center, The Steadman Clinic, Vail-Summit Orthopedics & Neurosurgery, Anesthesia Partners Colorado, Cardinal Pathology, Critical Care & Pulmonary Consults, Obstetrics/Pediatrics at Vail Health Hospital excluding CMM providers, Dillon Surgery Center, Steadman Philippon Surgery Center) are excluded.
Financial counselors assist patients in determining eligibility for government-sponsored programs and refer to Colorado health insurance exchange.

After submitting completed application with supporting documentation, patient receives eligibility letter within 60 days; Hospital Discounted Care letters within 14 days of receipt of completed application.
If application received within 240 days of initial billing and deemed incomplete, written notice sent within 15 days requesting missing information within 30 days of notice date.
Denials may be appealed with appeal letter and supporting documents; appeals reviewed within 30 days of receipt.
Once approved for financial assistance or Hospital Discounted Care, patient deemed approved for 12 months subsequent to approval.
If patient granted financial assistance on portion of bill and does not pay remaining portion, Vail Health will not reverse the amount of financial assistance granted.
Patients eligible at less than 250% FPL will not be charged more than amount collected from Vail Health's lowest commercial contracted payer.
Vail Health shall not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, sex, age or disability.
Full FAP and application form available at VailHealth.org/FinancialAssistance.

requires.label: Only Vail Health services eligible
requires.quote: The Vail Health financial assistance program is only applicable for Vail Health medical bills.

notes: Services conducted by a different medical provider other than Vail Health (even if performed in a Vail Health facility) fall outside of the policy scope and are not eligible for Vail Health financial assistance. Examples include Vail Valley Surgery Center, The Steadman Clinic, Vail-Summit Orthopedics & Neurosurgery, Anesthesia Partners Colorado (APC, Cardinal Pathology, Critical Care & Pulmonary Consults, Obstetrics/Pediatrics (Neonatal Nursey)-only services performed at Vail Health Hospital, excluding CMM providers. Services provided at the Vail Valley Surgery Center, Dillon Surgery Center and Steadman Philippon Surgery Center.

After submitting a completed application with requested supporting documentation, the patient will receive an eligibility letter from the Vail Health financial assistance department within 60 days. Patients eligible for Colorado’s Hospital Discounted Care will receive letters within 14 days of the receipt of the completed application

If a patient is granted financial assistance on a portion of the bill and the patient subsequently does not pay his/her remaining portion of the bill, Vail Health will not reverse the amount of financial assistance granted.

Once a patient has been approved for financial assistance or Hospital Discounted Care, the patient will be deemed to have approval for financial assistance towards services rendered by Vail Health for 12 months subsequent to approval.

Denials of financial assistance may be appealed. Appeals must include an appeal letter from the patient or party with financial responsibility requesting re-evaluation. The appeal must also include any supporting documents which were not part of the initial consideration that may prove inability to pay. Appeals will be referred to and reviewed by the financial counselors within 30 days of being received.

disagreements_before: A household of 3 earning $27,000 a year (98.8% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, uninsured, owing $10,000: the Nemotron 3 Ultra model gives no help, the Nemotron 3 Super model gives 100% off.

A household of 4 earning $123,000 a year (372.7% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, insured, and not under-insured as the policy defines it, owing $10,000: the Nemotron 3 Ultra model gives no help, the Nemotron 3 Super model gives 60% off.

A household of 5 earning $123,000 a year (318.0% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, insured, and not under-insured as the policy defines it, owing $10,000: the Nemotron 3 Ultra model gives no help, the Nemotron 3 Super model gives 80% off.

A household of 3 earning $123,000 a year (450.2% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, insured, and not under-insured as the policy defines it, owing $10,000, enrolled in SNAP, WIC or a similar program (or homeless): the Nemotron 3 Ultra model gives help (amount not stated), the Nemotron 3 Super model gives no help.
